Subject: Trail tips for your next stretch of miles
CTA: Read more trail tips on the blog -> https://www.northbaysupply.com/blog/trail-tips
Body: Hey,

You've been out there enough to know that the difference between a good trip and a rough one usually comes down to a handful of small decisions made before you leave the trailhead.

This season we're leaning into that. A few things worth thinking about before your next outing:

**Plan your water before you plan your miles.** Know your source intervals. A dry stretch of 8–10 miles changes your carry weight math entirely — plan for it, not around it.

**Layer for the descent, not the climb.** You'll be warm on the way up. The ridge is a different conversation. Pack accordingly.

**Know your bail points.** On any route longer than a day, identify two exit options before you start. Conditions change; having a plan means you're making a decision, not a reaction.

**Log your actual times, not your estimated ones.** After a few trips, your personal pace data is more useful than any trail app average.

One more thing — this is a game-changing season for us at Northbay Supply. We're not ready to say everything just yet, but we wanted you, our most engaged community, to hear it first when the time comes.

More soon. In the meantime, get out there.

— The Northbay Supply Team
